name: Orange 9mm
label: Revelation
lede: [[Chaka Malik]] brought a hatchet on stage with [[Burn]], guitarist [[Chris Traynor]] was in the crowd, and they set out to make hardcore that grooved like A Tribe Called Quest. Two major labels paid to find out whether it would sell.

eras.title: A hatchet at the Anthrax
eras.text: Burn was winding down when Malik met Traynor at a Burn show in Connecticut. Their blueprint was odd (A Tribe Called Quest, Smashing Pumpkins, Screaming Trees), and one EP for Revelation was enough to show what they meant.

years.big: "I had bought a hatchet that I brought out on stage with me."
years.h: A hatchet on stage at the Anthrax gets Chaka Malik a guitarist
years.p: Malik said that of a [[Burn|502429d5-da95-4a78-bfc9-7c8cf93504e6]] show at the Anthrax in Connecticut, where Chris Traynor was watching. The two planned a new band the same day.
years.xp:
Malik told No Echo that Traynor probably thought he was a little crazy. Burn was pretty much over by then, and the new band needed a target: "We picked three bands we wanted to model Orange 9mm after: A Tribe Called Quest, Smashing Pumpkins, and Screaming Trees."

The pitch was the good vibes of Tribe with the whimsy and heaviness of Pumpkins, plus Screaming Trees.

years.h: Fountainhead bandmate Larry Gorman takes the drum stool
years.p: Gorman comes in through Traynor, his bandmate in Fountainhead, with Eric Rice on bass. Gorman leaves soon after the EP is recorded, and when Rice quits, Davide Gentile takes the bass.

years.h: Orange 9mm EP lands on Revelation under a rhino · REV 31
years.p: After a demo with [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]], Revelation's Jordan Cooper tells the band to record as many songs as they can. Four tracks, cut fast, with a rhino photo by Chaka Malik's father, Jack Harris.
years.xp:
After labouring over lyrics in Burn, Malik changed his approach: "I said, 'Fuck this. I'm just gonna write.'" He wrote quickly and didn't worry what everything meant.

Revelation's pressing notes say a little under half of the 300 color copies came out salmon rather than orange/white swirl, and a later run of 553 dark green had three light green strays, a plant mistake.

eras.title: Major-label money, then the shelf
eras.text: One EP got Orange 9mm a deal with EastWest and a producer, Dave Jerden, who'd made records for Alice in Chains and Jane's Addiction. Tours with the new heavy bands followed. Sales fell short, and the label shelved them.

q: The EP sounds nothing like the album.
years.src: Wikipedia: Driver Not Included · No Echo
years.h: Dave Jerden produces Driver Not Included for EastWest
years.p: Cut at El Dorado in Los Angeles and Right Track in New York, with Davide Gentile on bass and Matthew Cross on drums. It reaches No. 17 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp: AllMusic called it a very strong effort that belongs among the important '90s aggro and hardcore records. Malik has been harder on it, telling No Echo the album was trying to be something the band wasn't.

years.h: Tours with Helmet, Korn and Deftones put a hardcore band on metal bills
years.p: Orange 9mm share stages with Helmet, Korn and Deftones in the mid-'90s, and tour with [[Ned's Atomic Dustbin|5ecee847-839a-4b9e-aae1-0e3b5dcea2ea]].

years.h: EastWest shelves the band, then hands it to Atlantic
years.p: Driver Not Included sells below expectations, per Perfect Sound Forever, and EastWest shelves Orange 9mm before moving it over to Atlantic.

eras.title: Tragic, and Helmet takes the guitarist
eras.text: Atlantic gave the band a second shot with Barkmarket's Dave Sardy producing. Tragic was their most acclaimed record, and within weeks Traynor, its main songwriter on guitar, had joined Helmet. A year later Atlantic let them go.

years.p: Recorded across three New York studios, including Chung King. Traynor plays most of the bass after Gentile's exit, and Taylor McLam joins near the end of the sessions.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Tragic reached No. 44 on the Heatseekers chart and sold over 47,000 copies in the US. Perfect Sound Forever calls it the band's most acclaimed record with poor sales to match.

The sound moved toward rap metal, with 7 and Method among the fan favorites.

years.big: "When Chris got asked to play with Helmet, he jumped at it. I was torn."
years.h: Chris Traynor takes the Helmet call mid-promotion
years.p: Taylor McLam on Traynor's exit shortly after Tragic comes out. McLam moves to guitar to cover.

years.h: Atlantic drops Orange 9mm with the tour support unpaid
years.p: Two albums in, Atlantic lets the band go. McLam's account: tour support was never paid back.
years.xp: McLam told Perfect Sound Forever that two major-label records without paying back the tour support left a band so in the hole it couldn't climb out. Orange 9mm kept going on an independent label.

eras.title: Rapping over loops, then done
eras.text: Orange 9mm landed on an indie, Ng Records, and swapped hardcore for rapping over loops and electronics. It didn't sell, the touring wore everyone down, and the band split in 2000.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pretend I'm Human · Perfect Sound Forever · Decibel
years.h: Every demo goes in the bin for Pretend I'm Human · Ng Records
years.p: Malik, McLam and Cross start fresh at Mad Dog in Burbank with producer Neil Perry. Malik plays bass himself.
years.xp: Recorded March to April 1999, with Sacha Jenkins on backing vocals. The Ultraman vs. Godzilla EP also came out on Ng around this time. Malik later described the album to Decibel as "a search for the new". Wikipedia calls it a commercial disappointment.

years.h: Warped Tour and Machine Head dates carry the new album
years.p: Orange 9mm tour Pretend I'm Human on the 1999 Warped Tour and on dates with [[Machine Head|22a1f4d7-81ff-4216-ac06-3387da6bc118]].

q: The music business can beat you down.
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · No Echo · Wikipedia: Orange 9mm
years.h: McLam: "We weren't feeling it." Orange 9mm call it quits
years.p: McLam saw no light at the end of the tunnel. Malik later put it as three albums with nine different sounds.

eras.title: Ghost Decibels and the remasters
eras.text: Traynor went on to Helmet and later Bush. Taylor McLam moved into commercial music and started High Desert Fires with Traynor. Malik came back with an electronic project, and the Orange 9mm records started coming back out.

years.h: Ghost Decibels brings Malik back to music
years.p: Orange 9mm's singer returns with an electronic project.

years.h: Pretend I'm Human comes back with the guitars turned up
years.p: RevHQ Records and Thirty Something Records remaster Orange 9mm's last album, fixing what Malik always said was wrong with it.
years.xp:
Malik told Decibel: "the guitars were just too low and it just wasn't a very impactful sounding record." Of the reissue: "the reissue has really brought us much closer to where I would have wanted to be."

He also made clear which band this is: "Orange 9 is more of a rock band than an electronic band. We need the hairy edges."

years.cap: Orange 9mm on the Terminal 5 rooftop, NYC Tattoo Convention
years.h: The late Ultraman vs. Godzilla EP gets a 2023 remaster
years.p: Orange 9mm's Ng Records EP arrives on streaming services in a new remaster.

eras.title: Twenty-five years later, on a rooftop
eras.text: Malik and McLam brought Orange 9mm back with a new rhythm section. Traynor, still in Bush, wasn't part of it.

years.cap: Orange 9mm on the Terminal 5 rooftop, New York, July 26, 2024
yt: Full set at Rich Hall Forever, June 2025
years.h: Cory Bonfiglio and Chris Enríquez become the new rhythm section
years.p: Malik and McLam announce the reunion, with Bonfiglio on bass and Enríquez on drums. Traynor stays in Bush.

years.cap: Orange 9mm on the Terminal 5 rooftop, New York, July 26, 2024
years.h: Twenty-five years after their last show, a rooftop at a tattoo convention
years.p: Orange 9mm play the Terminal 5 rooftop during the New York City Tattoo Arts Convention, their first show since 1999.
years.xp:
Stereogum lists Integrity, Into Another and Earth Crisis among the hardcore bands on the weekend's bill, with the band playing July 26 to 28.

Malik's announcement looked back at the start: "Tribe Called Quest, Screaming Trees, and Smashing Pumpkins were the influence."
